title: Choose the InboxOps composition
question: All three use the approved One-Bit Workstation world. Choose the structure that should govern the whole application.

options.label: Command Desk
options.thesis: Accounts, messages, and the active thread remain visible together for the fastest context switching.
options.viewport: A full-height account rail, broad inbox ledger, persistent reader, and integrated operations strip.
options.case: Best all-round familiarity and feature visibility across personal and work Gmail.
options.risk: The lower operations band can make laptop screens feel crowded.

options.label: Message Console
options.thesis: A dominant message ledger and layered reading sheet turn email processing into a fast focused flow.
options.viewport: The ledger owns the screen while the selected thread arrives as a strong right-side work sheet.
options.case: Strongest technical personality and keyboard workflow, with less room for secondary tools.
options.risk: The console metaphor can feel intimidating to casual Gmail users.

options.label: Operations Canvas
options.lineage: automation control rooms and modern mail workspaces
options.thesis: A calm message ledger shares the workspace with daily briefing, tasks, calendar actions, and AI provenance.
options.viewport: A daily briefing leads into a two-zone inbox and context-sensitive operations or reading workspace.
options.case: Best expression of InboxOps as more than email while remaining clear to first-time portfolio visitors.
options.risk: Secondary operations must collapse intelligently on laptop and mobile layouts.
